title: How the knots' bracketing decides the second fill
claim: The fewest-knot betweenness presentations of a line of n are exactly its bracketings (n - 2 knots, Catalan(n - 2) per arrangement). Under KF3 the first new distinction fills one knot uniformly (one knot set each); on a line with fills of triples there are two orders iff some fill exists and no fill's middle lies strictly inside another's span except at its own middle; after a first fill at kappa the options are the fills of the other knots and two re-bracketing fills per knot sharing a pair with kappa; hence P(two orders after the second new distinction) = (1/(n-2)) sum_kappa [s + 2p + c]/[(n - 3) + 2(p + c)], a function of the bare bracketing.
standard_statement: Minimal betweenness presentations of a path are polygon triangulations (rooted binary trees); an exact second-step formula for a knot-local Markov growth of split systems, read by lattice dimension.
